newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Strong dollar pushes Euro stocks to records.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Strong dollar pushes Euro stocks to records.

text.p: The dollar held firm on Tuesday as traders saw uncertainties in China and the Middle East as new reasons to buy, propelling European stock markets to record levels.

Shares rose across the continent in early trade, with many dealers citing the dollar's surge against the mark on Monday. But trade was muted as European markets awaited guidance from Wall Street, which reopens at 1430 GMT after a long weekend.
For once, currency dealers spoke less about interest rates and more about two fresh factors, the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and trouble in the Middle East.

News that top Chinese officials were hurriedly returning to Beijing from trips outside the capital shook Asian stock markets as investors feared that the 93-year-old Deng, who led China's economic reforms, might die soon.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry said there had been no major change in Deng's health. But dealers said the possibility of Chinese instability was a reason to buy dollars.

The Middle East weighed in, with Tehran Radio reporting that Iranian security forces had clashed with members of an Iraq-based opposition group, killing three and wounding another. But Iraq denied reports that it was massing troops near its border with Kuwait.
The dollar pushed ahead to 1.7020 marks from 1.6997 at Monday's European close while it was stable at 124.52 yen, little changed from Monday's 124.50.

Dealers said the buying reflected jittery markets wondering whether central banks would intervene to slow the dollar's rise against the mark and yen following last weekend's meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors from the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.

"Since G7 all the talk seems to have been about central bank intervention even though it wasn't even discussed at the meeting," said one trader. "This is making people nervous but when an excuse comes along to buy dollars they grab it with both hands."

While interest rates slipped from the top of traders' concerns, already worries are growing before U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan gives his Humphrey Hawkins testimony to Congress on February 27.

Away from the the dollar, the lira skidded almost half a percentage point amid concern that Italy might not make the first wave of European monetary union. The lira was at 989.70 to the mark, compared with 987.25 late on Monday.
On equity markets, London's FTSE 100 index was up 8.5 points at 4,346.3 points, only just short of an all-time high.

Traders awaited Wall Street for direction but one uncertainty disappeared for the time being at least when the Conservative government survived a parliamnetary censure on Monday night which could have led to a confidence vote and an early election.
"Without any lead from Wall Street it's difficult to see a great deal going on," said the head of sales at a U.S. investment bank in London.
In Paris and Frankfurt the dollar's strength, which helps European exporters, snuffed out the modest profit taking seen early on Monday and pushed shares to record levels.
Germany's DAX index was up 42.37 points or 1.31 percent at 3,274.94 while in Paris, the CAC-40 gained 18.91 (0.72 percent) to 3,274.94.

"The dollar is still the engine for the gains," said one Frankfurt dealer. Good bank results also helped to push up prices, although traders said the market still needed a consolidation after this year's heady gains.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7020 marks and 124.52 yen compared with 1.6997 marks and 124.50 yen in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 8.5 points at 4,346.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 18.91 at 2,653.39 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 42.37 points higher at 3,274.94.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $346.00 an ounce after closing on Monday at $344.25. Silver was at up three cents at $5.24.
